blocks.orig: Tanga in northern Tanzania is the regional headquarter and one of the largest cities in the country. Compared to Arusha or Moshi it is a rather quiet city, but with a comparable population. The city of Tanga is located on the Indian Ocean near the border with Kenya.
blocks.html: Tanga, in the north of Tanzania, serves as a regional headquarter and ranks among the biggest cities in the country. Its population is similar to that of Arusha or Moshi, yet the city feels considerably calmer. Tanga lies on the Indian Ocean, close to the Kenyan border.

blocks.orig: The name Tanga comes from the word “sail” because the port and its surrounding area is still the center of life in Tanga today. The most important export goods from the port include sisal, coffee, tea and cotton. The Portugese already used it as a  trading hub. They controlled the region around Tanga between 1500 and 1700. After that, the Sultanate of Oman gained control of the settlement. The city was a trading port for ivory and slaves until slavery was abolished by the European powers in 1873. In 1891 the Germans bought the Tanzanian coastline Mainland off the Sultan of Zanzibar. It became the first settlement in German East Africa and was the center of German colonial administration. Later Dar es Salaam was founded in the early 20th century.
blocks.html: The name Tanga is derived from the word “sail”, since the port and the area around it remain the heart of life in Tanga to this day. Sisal, coffee, tea and cotton are among the main goods exported from the port. Even the Portugese used it as a trading hub, ruling the region around Tanga from 1500 to 1700. The Sultanate of Oman then took over the settlement. Ivory and slaves were traded through the port until the European powers abolished slavery in 1873. In 1891 the Germans purchased the Tanzanian Mainland coastline from the Sultan of Zanzibar. Tanga became the first settlement of German East Africa and served as the hub of German colonial administration. Dar es Salaam was only founded later, in the early 20th century.

blocks.orig: As a coastal city, Tanga was on the forefront at the beginning of World War I with British East Africa (Kenya). After the war Great Britain took control of Tanganyika and the city developed further and used its agricultural potential. The port of Tanga continued to be a gateway for the export of sisal from the region in the early stages of independence from 1961. However, with the government’s control of agricultural trade and the devaluation of world market prices for sisal. The port of Tanga began to lose revenue.
blocks.html: Being on the coast, Tanga found itself on the front line with British East Africa (Kenya) when World War I broke out. Once the war was over, Great Britain took charge of Tanganyika, and the city grew and made use of its agricultural potential. In the early years of independence from 1961, the port of Tanga remained a gateway for exporting the region’s sisal. However, with the government taking control of agricultural trade and world market prices for sisal falling. The port of Tanga started to lose revenue.

blocks.orig: Today, despite its size, Tanga is a pleasant place with a sleepy, semi-colonial atmosphere, wide streets full of cyclists and motorbikes, fascinating architecture and faded charm.
blocks.html: Despite its size, Tanga today is an agreeable place with faded charm, fascinating architecture, a sleepy, semi-colonial feel and wide streets busy with cyclists and motorbikes.

blocks.orig: The best way to see the city’s beautiful, eclectic architecture is on a bike tour. Rent one of the heavy Chinese bikes! South of Tanga, along the maze of sandy paths of the Ras Kazone Peninsula, you’ll find fabulous Art Deco mansions, some of which are crumbling but others are lovingly cared for and testify to Tanga’s glorious days of sisal trading. Near the sea, houses stand side by side with the imposing colonial houses of the higher-ranking members of the British Empire. The original Bombo Hospital, right on the main road to Ras Kazone, stands out like a castle in a fairy tale. The hospital, built by the Germans, has since long fallen into disrepair and is now home to many birds. Stand in the empty halls amoung creeping plants and enjoy the nostalgic feeling of a bygone era.
blocks.html: A bike tour is the ideal way to take in the city’s lovely, eclectic architecture. Hire one of the sturdy Chinese bikes! To the south of Tanga, along the tangle of sandy paths on the Ras Kazone Peninsula, there are wonderful Art Deco mansions; some are crumbling, while others are carefully looked after and bear witness to Tanga’s heyday of sisal trading. Close to the sea, ordinary houses sit next to the grand colonial residences of senior members of the British Empire. On the main road to Ras Kazone, the original Bombo Hospital rises up like a fairy-tale castle. Built by the Germans, the hospital fell into disrepair long ago and now shelters many birds. Stand among the creeping plants in its empty halls and soak up the nostalgic feel of an era long gone.

blocks.orig: There are many examples of much older Arabic-style buildings found in Tanga: richly decorated mahogany balconies, meter-high walls, colored glass windows and heavy, dark doors, inner courtyards in which cats sneak around between deep shadows. If you feel too hot while cycling, look for the shade of a mango tree: there will likely be someone there selling you cups of hot, sweet espresso and slices of delicious kashata, a type of peanut fondant.
blocks.html: Tanga also has plenty of far older buildings in Arabic style: ornately decorated mahogany balconies, walls a metre high, coloured glass windows and heavy, dark doors, and inner courtyards where cats slip around in the deep shadows. Should you get too hot on the bike, find the shade of a mango tree: chances are someone there will sell you cups of hot, sweet espresso and slices of tasty kashata, a kind of peanut fondant.

Mkomazi National Park is a 4-5 hour drive from Tanga.
blocks.html: From Tanga, Mkomazi National Park is a drive of 4-5 hours.

blocks.orig: Often overlooked by travelers, Pangani is a wonderful find just 50 km south of Tanga! Only an hour drive away…
blocks.html: Just 50 km south of Tanga, Pangani is a lovely discovery that travelers often miss! It is only an hour’s drive away…

blocks.orig: And the Usambara Mountains are about 3 hours’ drive (110 km) west of Tanga.
blocks.html: The Usambara Mountains, meanwhile, lie roughly 3 hours’ drive (110 km) to the west of Tanga.

blocks.html: The drive to Bagamoyo takes 4.5 hrs, and reaching Dar Es Salaam takes 6 hrs.
